question: A 45-year-old male is presenting for routine health maintenance. He has no complaints. His pulse if 75/min, blood pressure is 155/90 mm Hg, and respiratory rate is 15/min. His body mass index is 25 kg/m2. The physical exam is within normal limits. He denies any shortness of breath, daytime sleepiness, headaches, sweating, or palpitations. He does not recall having an elevated blood pressure measurement before. Which of the following is the best next step?
analysis: The best next step in this scenario would be to repeat the blood pressure measurement to confirm the elevated reading. It is important to rule out white coat hypertension or other factors that may have influenced the initial reading.
